background_rationale: A CPA who built his early career as a treasurer and chief financial officer of health care companies, including six years as CFO of US Oncology, before moving into CEO roles.

notable.summary: Took over as HP's interim CEO effective immediately after Enrique Lores resigned; the board formed a search committee and hired an executive search firm to find a permanent CEO.
Reporting fiscal second-quarter revenue of $14.4 billion, up 9%, Broussard pointed to new AI PCs, Z workstations, AI-powered print and HP IQ as HP managed rising commodity costs.
HP raised its fiscal 2026 EPS and free cash flow guidance after third-quarter revenue rose 12.5% to $15.7 billion, with Broussard describing HP as a trusted edge platform for AI.

personal_story.hook: Bruce Broussard ran health insurer Humana for over a decade before stepping in as HP's interim CEO in 2026.
personal_story.summary: Broussard was born in Hamilton, New York; his father served in the U.S. Air Force and later worked in telecommunications, and after several moves the family settled in Houston. He studied accounting and finance at Texas A&M, earned an MBA in finance at the University of Houston and became a CPA. He spent his early career in health care finance roles, then rose from CFO to CEO and chairman at US Oncology and led Humana from 2013 to 2024. A member of HP's board since 2021, he was named interim CEO in February 2026 when Enrique Lores left.
